towers.name: ŘLP planned remote tower centre, Mošnov (Ostrava)
towers.note: Planned. In August 2023 the ŘLP chief said it should open in two to three years; a later report says construction had not started and an operational concept was still being drafted. No vendor is named.

dates.t: ŘLP chief says remote tower in Ostrava targeted within two to three years

facts.t: ŘLP, the Czech air navigation provider, plans a remote tower at Mošnov near Ostrava to control České Budějovice, which could later serve other regional airports.

A later Zdopravy.cz report says the stated deadline had passed, construction had not started at either site, and an operational concept and cost-benefit analysis come first. A floor of the Mošnov control tower was reserved in 2016.

towers.name: České Budějovice Airport
towers.note: Planned only. No vendor named and no approval or contract found.

dates.t: ŘLP confirms it is considering a remote tower for the airport

facts.t: Aeroweb.cz, 1 September 2022: ŘLP was considering a remote virtual tower for České Budějovice within three to four years; no vendor is named.
Zdopravy.cz, 19 August 2023: all traffic including taxiing and parking would be controlled from Ostrava, probably starting as an on-request service.

towers.name: Amami Airport (remote aerodrome air-ground service)
towers.note: This is a remote aerodrome air-ground (RADIO) service from Naha, not remote air traffic control. Japan has no remote tower providing control service in the sources reviewed.

dates.t: Remote RADIO operation from Naha begins (Japan's first)
OKI announces delivery of the RVA-19 system to the Civil Aviation Bureau

facts.t: OKI says Amami began remote RADIO operation on 1 October 2021, with a flight information officer at Naha Airport providing air-ground service through its RVA-19 remote tower device.
A July 2021 trade report describes Japan's remote tower work as research at the Electronic Navigation Research Institute, with a small remote air-ground system serving some low-traffic airports.

towers.name: skeyes digital tower control centre, Namur
towers.note: Plotted at Namur; exact site approximate.

dates.t: Building completed
Planned to become operational (equipped in 2026)

facts.t: skeyes says the Namur building was completed in 2025, will be further equipped in 2026 and become operational in 2027; Liège and Charleroi will be controlled from it.
Charleroi and Liège are the first skeyes airports to get digital towers, controlled from Namur from 2027.

towers.name: skeyes Digital Tower Test Centre, Steenokkerzeel
towers.note: Plotted near Brussels Airport; exact site approximate.

dates.t: Digital Tower Test Centre unveiled

facts.t: Saab's 31 May 2024 release says skeyes unveiled a Digital Tower Test Centre in Steenokkerzeel, a prototype for the Namur centre, built on Saab's Remote Tower solution, for training controllers.

dates.t: Searidge and AIN report the virtual tower in operational service

facts.t: AIN, 1 December 2025: Hamad's virtual tower, built on Searidge's Chorus platform, 'has entered operational service' under a hybrid model adopted by the Qatar CAA; two positions are in the main tower and two in the backup and approach training centre.
NATS lists Hamad as a certified hybrid digital tower and the first large-scale digital tower certified by safety regulators in the Middle East.

towers.name: Qaqortoq Airport (new, local digital tower)
towers.note: Plotted at Qaqortoq town; exact site approximate. Frequentis says similar systems are already in place at Nuuk and Ilulissat, but gives no dates, so those are not listed here.

facts.t: Frequentis was awarded a contract (via the construction firm COMSA) for a Local Digital Tower at the new Qaqortoq airport; it describes a vision of centralised control from Nuuk.

towers.name: Invercargill Airport
towers.note: Contract awarded in 2019 with go-live expected in 2020. No go-live notice found.

dates.t: Airways awards Frequentis the contract for the first New Zealand digital tower

facts.t: Airways New Zealand awarded Frequentis a contract for a remotely operated digital tower at Invercargill; controllers would start at the airfield and later move to a hub, with operation expected by 2020.

towers.name: Buenos Aires Ezeiza International Airport
towers.note: Vendor page only; customer and dates not stated. Treat as unconfirmed.

facts.t: Frequentis says Ezeiza will receive an airport camera system as a first step toward what it calls South America's first remote virtual tower, with tower control to follow completion of a new tower.

towers.name: Chizhou Jiuhuashan Airport (remote tower trial)
towers.note: A trial under the CAAC. The paper does not name a vendor.

dates.t: Remote tower optical system installed

facts.t: A Chinese paper to ICAO describes a remote tower optical system installed at Chizhou in September 2021 and operated from the Anhui ATC Bureau about 180 km away; trial operations, with full remote service planned after trial and transition phases.

towers.name: Xinyuan Nalati Airport (remote tower trial)
towers.note: One report, May 2020; no later notice found.

dates.t: China Express flight controlled remotely from Urumqi in what Aviation Week called China's first remote tower operation

facts.t: Aviation Week, 22 May 2020: a China Express Airlines flight was controlled remotely from the Xinjiang Airport Group's centre in Urumqi, 385 km away, at Xinyuan Nalati.

towers.name: Miquelon Airport (remote from Saint-Pierre)
towers.note: Selected in 2016. NATS lists a Miquelon and Saint-Pierre digital tower as a reference, while a union document calls earlier French attempts failures. Neither gives a service date.

dates.t: DSNA selects Searidge's remote tower for Miquelon, to be controlled from Saint-Pierre

facts.t: DSNA selected Searidge in March 2016 to remote Miquelon from Saint-Pierre, about 40 km away; cameras to be installed at Miquelon.
NATS's digital tower page lists Miquelon and Saint-Pierre as a digital tower where controllers manage both airfields remotely from one location; no date is given.
